title: A million streams, no rent
name: HSW365 MEDIA

scenes.say: Two in the morning. Another song done. Another drop for the streams.
A million plays. Check comes in. Barely covers the light bill.
scenes.visual: close up of a hand holding a smartphone in a dark recording studio showing a music streaming payout screen with a tiny dollar amount, red studio light glow, shallow depth of field, gritty cinematic commercial photography

scenes.say: Then a fan hits my DMs. Where can I buy your music direct? I want the shirt too.
scenes.visual: cinematic photo, young woman in a hoodie on her bed at night smiling at her phone, typing a message, warm lamp light and phone glow on her face, candid film still, vertical portrait composition

scenes.say: That's when it hit me. The fans were never the problem. I had no store.
So I had HSW365 Media build my own page. My music, my merch, my shows. One link.
scenes.visual: hero shot of a smartphone held up in a dark studio showing a sleek black artist website with album covers, a merch section with hoodies and a concert tickets button, red and cyan glow, premium tech commercial product photography, crisp detail

scenes.say: No middleman. No algorithm. The fans pay me. Straight to my account.
scenes.visual: cinematic photo, a packed small concert crowd at night holding up phones with screen glow, fans wearing matching black band hoodies, red stage light haze, energetic film still, vertical portrait composition

scenes.say: First weekend, I sold more off my page than a year of streams.
scenes.visual: close up of a work table covered in shipping boxes and folded black hoodies with packing slips, a laptop showing a list of new orders in the background, warm studio light, lifestyle advertising photography, vertical portrait composition

scenes.say: Artists, stop renting your fans. Own them. Scan the code. Build your page with HSW365 Media.

caption:
A million streams and the check barely covers the light bill. Then a fan asks where to buy direct, and it hits: the fans were never the problem. There was no store.

Artists: build your own page. Your music, your merch, your shows, one link, and your fans pay you directly. No middleman, no algorithm.
